relationship_to_protagonist: The wealthy match his father requires, and the marriage he unaccountably consents to after his character changes.
relationship_to_romance: The competing claim, and dynastic rather than emotional.
character_gist: The rich woman Balbir Singh wants his son to marry, and whom the transformed Ganga becomes willing to wed.

relationship_to_protagonist: The deposed and murdered raja, father of the twins and uncle of the prince; the double role rests on his line.
relationship_to_romance: No part in it.
character_gist: A fair-minded ruler overthrown by his own brother, whose twin sons are ordered killed and who is then killed with his wife in a staged road accident.

relationship_to_protagonist: His mother and the usurper's wife, inside the household the coup created.
relationship_to_romance: Part of the family front against a poor bride.
character_gist: Balbir Singh's wife and Ganga's mother, pregnant at the time of the coup along with the raja's wife.

relationship_to_protagonist: Plays both of Kapoor's identities as children, so the double role is doubled again in the child section; he is Kapoor's own son.
relationship_to_romance: No part in it.
character_gist: The childhood of both Ganga and Jwala Singh, played by Kapoor's elder son, two years after his appearance as Siddhartha's son.

relationship_to_protagonist: The film's protagonist, and the man whose girlfriend Kapoor's businessman takes; the two never contend directly, which is the point.
relationship_to_romance: Holds the claim Kapoor's character displaces. Sheetal loves Bharat and marries Mohan.
character_gist: An unemployed graduate supporting his family on a singer's pay, who loses his building job to a government takeover, watches his girlfriend marry a rich man, burns his diploma on his father's pyre, and takes work with a corrupt businessman before turning informer.

relationship_to_protagonist: His secretary, then his wife: she accepts Kapoor's Mohan while loving Bharat, which is the film's hardest transaction.
relationship_to_romance: The pairing recorded in the Romances sheet, and secondary to the film's argument about poverty: the marriage is an economic decision rather than a courtship.
character_gist: Bharat's girlfriend, frustrated by his low pay, who takes a secretary's job with the businessman Mohan Babu, cannot contemplate a life in poverty, and accepts Mohan's proposal.

relationship_to_protagonist: No dealings with Kapoor's Mohan; the two occupy separate strands of the same film, a year before Deewaar paired them directly.
relationship_to_romance: Outside it.
character_gist: Bharat's younger brother, who turns to crime to provide for the family, quarrels with Bharat and joins the army, and returns to help him bring down Nekiram.

relationship_to_protagonist: No dealings with Mohan Babu; he is the antagonist of Bharat's strand.
relationship_to_romance: No part in it.
character_gist: A corrupt businessman who recruits the desperate Bharat for his illegal work and frames him when Bharat decides to inform the police.

relationship_to_protagonist: Outside Mohan Babu's strand.
relationship_to_romance: The counterweight to Sheetal in the film's scheme: the poor woman Bharat helps, against the one who leaves him for money.
character_gist: A woman living in poverty whom Bharat helps and in helping finds some salvation, and whose rescue from a gang brings Harnam Singh into his life.

relationship_to_protagonist: Outside Mohan Babu's strand.
relationship_to_romance: No part in it.
character_gist: A sardar who comes to Bharat's rescue when he tries to save Tulsi from a gang of hoodlums, and becomes his friend.

relationship_to_protagonist: The one family member the film gives Kapoor's businessman, in a part the synopsis does not develop.
relationship_to_romance: The household Sheetal marries into.
character_gist: Credited as the mother of Kapoor's Mohan Babu, the sole domestic detail the film attaches to the rich man's side of the story.

relationship_to_protagonist: His sweetheart, and his equal in poverty: both are supporting families on nothing when the job offer comes.
relationship_to_romance: The pairing recorded in the Romances sheet: a couple whose enemy is money, and who lose their moral bearings together rather than against each other.
character_gist: A young woman scraping for pennies to nurse her ailing mother while her father drinks his earnings, sweetheart to a man in the same condition, and drawn with him into a world of wealth that costs them both their moral compass.

relationship_to_protagonist: Third-billed, in the world of wealth and intrigue the job takes him into; the article's four-sentence synopsis does not detail the part.
relationship_to_romance: Not documented, though the billing places her opposite the established couple.
character_gist: Credited as Rashmi. The article's plot summary runs to four sentences and names no character beyond Raj, Poonam and her.

relationship_to_protagonist: Not documented; the article gives no character name.
relationship_to_romance: Not documented.
character_gist: Credited without a character name, among the principals of the wealthy world the film's second half enters.

relationship_to_protagonist: Not documented; the article gives no character name.
relationship_to_romance: Not documented.
character_gist: Credited without a character name, alongside Kader Khan and Dina Pathak, in a cast list the article's brief synopsis does not map.

relationship_to_protagonist: Not documented; the article gives no character name.
relationship_to_romance: Not documented.
character_gist: Credited without a character name. The film turns on two families kept in poverty, but the article does not say which of them she belongs to.

relationship_to_protagonist: His elder brother, who sacrificed his own schooling to pay for Ravi's, and whom Ravi as a policeman must finally hunt and shoot; the film is the argument between them.
relationship_to_romance: Outside Ravi's romance. His own attachment to Anita runs parallel and ends in her death.
character_gist: The elder son, tattooed as a boy with his father's supposed disgrace, who refuses the temple, rises from shoeshiner and dockworker to smuggler under Daavar, and is killed by his brother's bullet after their mother chooses Ravi's side.

relationship_to_protagonist: His mother, who leaves Vijay's house to live with Ravi, and whose choice supplies the moral sanction for everything Ravi does after.
relationship_to_romance: No part in it.
character_gist: The mother who brings both sons to Bombay after her husband's disgrace and flight, raises them on a building site and under a bridge, and finally sides with the policeman against the smuggler.

relationship_to_protagonist: Ravi's romance, and the daughter of the DCP he serves under; the courtship runs through the household of his own authority.
relationship_to_romance: The pairing recorded in the Romances sheet, and minor in the film: the romance is light relief inside a story about two brothers.
character_gist: Daughter of DCP Narang, courted by the unemployed and then newly commissioned Ravi, in the one strand of the film conducted in a comic register.

relationship_to_protagonist: No dealings with Ravi; she belongs wholly to Vijay's side of the film.
relationship_to_romance: The other romance, and the tragic one against which Ravi's courtship is measured.
character_gist: The woman who attaches herself to Vijay at the height of his power, carries his child, and is killed by Samant's men, taking from him the last thing he had outside the feud.

relationship_to_protagonist: His father, who abandoned the family before Ravi was old enough to know him, and whose disgrace shaped Vijay rather than Ravi.
relationship_to_romance: No part in it.
character_gist: A principled trade union leader blackmailed into signing away his labourers' rights to save his kidnapped family, beaten by the men he led, and lost to a life of aimless travel by train.

relationship_to_protagonist: The father of the boy Ravi shoots for stealing bread, and so the author of Ravi's one real crisis of conscience about the law he serves.
relationship_to_romance: No part in it.
character_gist: A schoolteacher whose hungry son Ravi shoots while on duty, and who tells the policeman he did right, in the scene that sets Ravi's creed against his own doubt.

relationship_to_protagonist: His superior officer and Veera's father, the two facts that make Ravi's position untenable once the quarry is his own brother.
relationship_to_romance: Governs it, being the father of the woman Ravi is courting.
character_gist: The deputy commissioner who commands Ravi and whose daughter he is courting, and who gives him the assignment against the smuggler he cannot name.

relationship_to_protagonist: The smuggler whose organisation Ravi is set against, and Vijay's patron; he is the reason the brothers end on opposite sides.
relationship_to_romance: No part in it.
character_gist: The smuggling boss who recruits the dockworker Vijay after seeing him fight, raises him to be his right hand, and is killed in the war with Samant.

relationship_to_protagonist: No dealings with Ravi; he is the rival Vijay destroys, and the man whose retaliation kills Anita.
relationship_to_romance: Destroys Vijay's, by having Anita killed.
character_gist: Daavar's rival smuggler, whose war with Vijay costs Daavar his life and Vijay the woman carrying his child.

relationship_to_protagonist: His best friend, whom he shelters as a wanted revolutionary without knowing the man was his own wife's lover; the friendship and the marriage are the same crisis.
relationship_to_romance: The prior claim on Kapoor's wife, and the reason the marriage is poisoned by a police file rather than by anything either spouse does.
character_gist: An apolitical poet who turns revolutionary after his freedom-fighter brother is shot, pretends to Kamini that he only used her as material for his verse so she will not be widowed, kills British officials, and takes refuge in the house of the friend who has married her.

relationship_to_protagonist: His bride, who was Rajesh's sweetheart and is hostile to the fugitive in her house; the marriage is new when the crisis arrives.
relationship_to_romance: The pairing recorded in the Romances sheet as a triangle, and the one whose terms neither man will state aloud.
character_gist: Daughter of a Rai Bahadur in British service, sweetheart of the poet Rajesh, told by him that she was only material for his poems, married to his best friend, and made to recite with him the poem in which he admits breaking her heart.

relationship_to_protagonist: Brings the wounded fugitive to Kapoor's door, and is the man Kapoor then lies to Rajesh about; billed as a guest appearance.
relationship_to_romance: No part in it, though his death is the lie that sits between the two friends.
character_gist: A Pathan truck driver who carries the wounded Rajesh to Dheeraj's house, is tortured by a constable seeking the revolutionary's whereabouts, and kills himself saying Rajesh lives in his heart.

relationship_to_protagonist: Rajesh's elder brother rather than Dheeraj's kin; his death converts the poet into the fugitive Dheeraj must hide.
relationship_to_romance: No part in it.
character_gist: A freedom fighter, elder brother of the poet, shot dead by British officials during a demonstration, whose killing turns Rajesh to the armed struggle.

relationship_to_protagonist: Kamini's father, and the reason she was never going to be given to a Gandhian household.
relationship_to_romance: The original external opposition to Rajesh and Kamini, which is what leaves her free to marry Dheeraj.
character_gist: Kamini's father, who works for the British government and dislikes the Narayan family for working for Gandhi.

relationship_to_protagonist: The one relative the film gives Kapoor's superintendent, in the household where the fugitive is hidden.
relationship_to_romance: A presence in the house where the triangle plays out.
character_gist: Credited as Dheeraj's aunty, in the police officer's household that shelters a wanted revolutionary.

relationship_to_protagonist: First-billed opposite Kapoor's Bhola in what the credits present as a two-man film. The article has no plot section, so the partnership is not documented.
relationship_to_romance: Not documented. Romance presence is left blank for the film for the same reason.
character_gist: Credited as Shankar and billed ahead of Kapoor. With no synopsis in the article the part is recorded from the cast list alone.

relationship_to_protagonist: The principal female part, credited with Chaman Puri as her father. The article gives no plot, so her relation to Bhola is unrecorded.
relationship_to_romance: Not documented, which is why no Romances row was created for the film.
character_gist: Credited as Sharmili, third-billed. The article carries a long cast list and no synopsis.

relationship_to_protagonist: Not documented, though the double credit of a policeman and a second identity implies the film's central deception.
relationship_to_romance: Not documented.
character_gist: A double credit as Inspector Kumar and Shera, with Asha Potdar as the inspector's wife. The article has no plot section to explain the doubling.

relationship_to_protagonist: Not documented.
relationship_to_romance: Not documented.
character_gist: Credited as Parvin Chandra Shah, in the comic register Deven Verma occupied in this period. The article gives no synopsis.

relationship_to_protagonist: Not documented.
relationship_to_romance: Not documented.
character_gist: Credited as Amarchand Rathod, with Urmila Bhatt as Parvati Rathod, a family unit the article does not place in any story.

relationship_to_protagonist: Not documented beyond the credit, which names him Sharmili's father.
relationship_to_romance: Not documented.
character_gist: Credited as Shambhu, Sharmili's father. The article's cast list is its only content on the story.

relationship_to_protagonist: The childhood neighbour from whom he was separated by his father's arrest, and the woman he meets and loves years later without either recognising the other.
relationship_to_romance: The whole of it, and the pairing recorded in the Romances sheet: friendship to love, with the friendship forgotten by both parties.
character_gist: A girl inseparable from the boy next door, separated from him when his father is arrested, grown into a professional stage singer and dancer under the name Seema, travelling to her birthplace on a religious errand when she meets and falls in love with the card-sharp she once knew as Raju.

relationship_to_protagonist: Billed high among the supporting cast around the thief's world.
relationship_to_romance: The comic accompaniment to a courtship built on two forgotten childhoods.
character_gist: Credited as Abdul Rehman, the comic lead of the supporting cast in a film about a card-sharp who gets himself jailed for money.

relationship_to_protagonist: Credited as Master, in the criminal apparatus around Chander; the article's synopsis breaks off before the jail scheme plays out.
relationship_to_romance: The danger the romance is conducted against.
character_gist: Credited as Master, among the film's criminal figures. The article's plot summary stops at Chander's plan to be jailed for a gangster's fee.

relationship_to_protagonist: The proprietor of the gambling world where the card-sharp works.
relationship_to_romance: No documented part in it.
character_gist: The casino owner in the world Raju has grown into as a card-sharp and thief.

relationship_to_protagonist: Seema's father, from the neighbourhood the two children shared.
relationship_to_romance: The family on her side of a reunion neither party knows is one.
character_gist: Credited as Ram Lal, Seema's father, belonging to the childhood neighbourhood the film's second half returns to.

relationship_to_protagonist: A guest appearance by Kapoor's own elder brother, billed as a cameo.
relationship_to_romance: No part in it.
character_gist: A truck driver, played as a cameo appearance by Shammi Kapoor, the middle of the three Kapoor brothers.

relationship_to_protagonist: The female lead opposite Kapoor's Karmu. The article describes the film as a romance and carries a cast list and a production section, but no plot, so the courtship is undocumented.
relationship_to_romance: The romance the article's genre description implies and never narrates, which is why no Romances row was created for the film.
character_gist: Credited as Nanki Mehto, of the Mehto family the cast list builds out with a mother, a Vaidraj and a Jaggu. The article gives no synopsis.

relationship_to_protagonist: Third-billed, so a substantial part, but the article carries no plot to place her against Karmu or Nanki.
relationship_to_romance: Not documented.
character_gist: Credited as Somu, third-billed. Whether the part is a second romantic interest or something else cannot be determined from the article.

character_gist: A childless wife who goes alone to her husband's Khandala bungalow, is pursued by the decorator she knew slightly at college, kills him accidentally in the struggle, disposes of the body with her sister's help, and finds him brought back into the house as an amnesiac patient.

relationship_to_protagonist: The husband of the woman he pursued, and the doctor whose professional competence is the threat: his treatment will restore the memory that condemns his own wife.
relationship_to_romance: The marriage the pursuit violates, and the instrument of the film's suspense.
character_gist: A wealthy doctor childless after years of marriage, who brings home a man claiming to have lost his memory, diagnoses a gradual recovery, and works towards the restoration that would expose his wife.

relationship_to_protagonist: The sister-in-law who hired him to decorate the bungalow, and who then helps dispose of his body.
relationship_to_romance: Sets the pursuit in motion by the hiring, and covers up its consequence.
character_gist: Aarti's sister, living near the Khandala bungalow, who engages Vinod to decorate it as a fellow she remembers from college, and afterwards helps her sister hide what she has done.

relationship_to_protagonist: Vidya's husband, in the household next to the bungalow where the killing happens.
relationship_to_romance: No part in it.
character_gist: A retired army major, Vidya's husband, with whom she lives near the Khandala bungalow along with their son Raju.

relationship_to_protagonist: A household presence around the bungalow.
relationship_to_romance: No part in it.
character_gist: Credited as Bahadur, with Preeti Ganguli as Rosie, the film's comic relief against a concealed killing.

relationship_to_protagonist: The other half of the pairing the title names, on a double credit matching Kapoor's own. The article has no plot section, so the relation is undocumented.

character_gist: A double credit as Bada Kumar and Shakti Singh, opposite Kapoor's Chhota Kumar and Amar Singh; the title Amar Shakti pairs the two second names. The article gives no synopsis.

relationship_to_protagonist: The princess of the film's court, opposite Kapoor; the article does not place her against either brother.
relationship_to_romance: Not documented, which is why no Romances row was created.
character_gist: Credited as Rajkumari Sunita Singh, third-billed. The article carries a long cast list of princely titles and no plot.

relationship_to_protagonist: The maharaja of a court in which Kapoor's character carries the name Amar Singh, which suggests the father, though the article does not confirm it.
relationship_to_romance: Not documented.
character_gist: Credited as Maharaj Shamsher Singh. With no plot section the article leaves the succession the film turns on unexplained.

relationship_to_romance: Not documented.
character_gist: Credited as Diwan Nahar Singh, the court minister of a princely drama whose plot the article does not record.

character_gist: Credited as the fencing guru of Kapoor's Amar, a part played by the swashbuckling star of an earlier generation.

relationship_to_romance: Not documented.
character_gist: Credited as Hameera, son of Om Shivpuri's Sardar Ajit Singh, in a court drama the article does not summarise.

relationship_to_protagonist: Not documented.
relationship_to_romance: Not documented.
character_gist: Credited as Chamki, fourth-billed, the second female part in a film whose article has no plot section.

relationship_to_protagonist: The wife he rejects on the wedding night and the mistress he courts by night, both the same woman; the film is his refusal to identify them.
relationship_to_romance: The pairing recorded in the Romances sheet: a marriage under strain in which the strain is entirely the husband's idea of beauty.
character_gist: A village priest's daughter whose face was scarred by boiling oil as a child, who sings at the temple behind her veil, is loved for her voice, tries to have the match refused, marries and is disowned on the wedding night, and is then courted veiled by the same husband until she is pregnant.

relationship_to_protagonist: No scenes with Kapoor's engineer; she plays the childhood accident that sets the whole story.
relationship_to_romance: Establishes the disfigurement the romance is built on refusing to see.
character_gist: Roopa as a child, whose right cheek and neck are burned by a pot of boiling oil, the injury she thereafter keeps under her sari.

relationship_to_protagonist: Roopa's father, the village priest, from whom Rajeev asks her hand, and who is pressed by the village into consenting to a marriage he knows is founded on a misunderstanding.
relationship_to_romance: Permits the deception the film turns on, and is asked by his own daughter to refuse the proposal first.
character_gist: The village priest, Roopa's father, approached for his daughter's hand by an engineer who has not seen her scarred side, asked by Roopa herself to reject the proposal, and talked round by the village.

relationship_to_protagonist: Roopa's uncle, part of the village household the engineer marries into.
relationship_to_romance: Among those who press the marriage forward.
character_gist: Credited as Bansi, Roopa's uncle, in the village family whose interest in the match overrides her own misgivings.

relationship_to_protagonist: Belongs to the dam works Rajeev has come to oversee.
relationship_to_romance: Peripheral to the marriage plot.
character_gist: Credited as Bade Babu, with Leela Chitnis as his wife, among the engineering establishment around the dam.

relationship_to_protagonist: Rajeev's superior on the dam project that brought him to the village.
relationship_to_romance: No part in it.
character_gist: The chief engineer over the major dam Rajeev arrives in the village to oversee.

relationship_to_protagonist: His elder brother, presumed dead with him in the sabotaged bus, grown up separately into a CID inspector.
relationship_to_romance: Outside Laxman's romance.
character_gist: The eldest of Harnam Prasad's three sons, thrown off a cliff in the sabotaged picnic bus and assumed dead, who grows up to be a CID inspector working under the alias Rocky.

relationship_to_protagonist: The youngest brother, taken the other way: a criminal fisherman working for the man who destroyed their family.
relationship_to_romance: Holds his own attachment to Poonam, whose mother Heeralal murdered.
character_gist: The third son, lost at sea with his father and waylaid into crime, now a criminal fisherman in Heeralal's service with Poonam as his accomplice, unaware whom he is working for.

relationship_to_protagonist: Kapoor's romantic partner, in a film whose business is the scattering and reassembly of a family.
relationship_to_romance: The pairing recorded in the Romances sheet, and subordinate to the revenge plot.
character_gist: Credited as Rekha, paired with Kapoor's Laxman Prasad, the factory worker among the three brothers.

relationship_to_protagonist: His father, and the cause of everything: it is his testimony as eyewitness that brings the gang's revenge down on his own family.
relationship_to_romance: No part in it.
character_gist: A devout customs officer who witnesses Heeralal's smuggling and his murder of a fisherwoman, testifies to both, and sees his wife crippled, his house burned and his three sons scattered in reprisal.

relationship_to_protagonist: His mother, who loses her legs in the fire set by the gang and believes all three sons dead.
relationship_to_romance: No part in it.
character_gist: Harnam's wife, attacked with kerosene fire that burns down the house and costs her both legs, saved from suicide by a woman who takes her into her own home.

relationship_to_protagonist: The smuggler whose revenge destroyed his family and who, released from jail, now employs his youngest brother.
relationship_to_romance: No part in it.
character_gist: A smuggler who kills a fisherwoman to stop her testimony, is jailed on Harnam's evidence, and on release runs gold and uranium with the dead woman's daughter and the youngest Prasad son in his employ.

relationship_to_protagonist: No documented dealings with Laxman; she is attached to the youngest brother's criminal strand.
relationship_to_romance: Holds the film's second attachment, with Bharat.
character_gist: Bharat's accomplice in Heeralal's service, and the daughter of the fisherwoman Heeralal murdered to silence her testimony.

relationship_to_protagonist: His half-brother, unacknowledged, who has come to Delhi specifically to ruin the business and family Shekhar has come home to join.
relationship_to_romance: Outside Shekhar's engagement, though he twice intervenes in the family's affairs in ways that touch it.
character_gist: The son Raj Kumar Gupta abandoned before birth, raised by a single mother whose death releases him, who arrives in Delhi to destroy his father's business, builds Shanti Constructions against it, and protects his half-siblings while wrecking their father.

relationship_to_protagonist: His father, and the man whose abandonment of another woman in 1953 is the cause of everything that happens to Shekhar.
relationship_to_romance: Governs the family Shekhar's marriage would join, and his ruin is what unsettles it.
character_gist: A man who abandoned his pregnant girlfriend in 1953 to marry a wealthy heiress and take a partnership in her father's firm, and who twenty-five years later is systematically destroyed in business by the son he never acknowledged.

relationship_to_protagonist: Kapoor's romantic partner, and the daughter of P. L. Verma, so the match is also a business alliance.
relationship_to_romance: The pairing recorded in the Romances sheet, and subordinate to the film's revenge plot.
character_gist: P. L. Verma's daughter, attached to the returning Shekhar Gupta, in a courtship conducted across the collapse of his father's firm.

relationship_to_protagonist: His father's devoted secretary, fired on a false suspicion that Shekhar witnesses being corrected.
relationship_to_romance: Holds the other romance, with Vijay, and is the point at which the two brothers' worlds first touch.
character_gist: Gupta's loyal secretary, who refuses Vijay's bribe, is dismissed when her employer assumes she sold him out, is publicly cleared by Vijay and then hired by him.

relationship_to_protagonist: His younger sister, caught with him in the crossfire of a half-brother's revenge.
relationship_to_romance: Carries the film's third romance, with Ravi.
character_gist: Shekhar's younger sister, called Babli, one of the two legitimate children whom Vijay's campaign against their father puts in the line of fire.

relationship_to_protagonist: No scenes with Shekhar; she is dead before he returns from abroad, and is the reason he has a half-brother at all.
relationship_to_romance: The abandoned romance of the previous generation, against which all three of the film's courtships are set. Billed as a special appearance.
character_gist: The woman Raj Kumar Gupta abandoned in 1953, who refused his guilty offer of help, bore and raised Vijay alone, and whose death in 1978 sets her son on Delhi; the company he builds carries her name.

relationship_to_protagonist: The film's criminal antagonist, outside the family quarrel that Shekhar is caught in.
relationship_to_romance: No direct part in it.
character_gist: Credited as Balwant Rai, the antagonist against whom the brothers' interests eventually align in a film otherwise about a family destroying itself.

relationship_to_protagonist: Sheetal's father, and so his prospective father-in-law, as well as a figure in the contracting world the two firms are fighting over.
relationship_to_romance: Governs the match from the woman's side.
character_gist: Sheetal's father, credited among the business interests around the tender bids that Vijay's firm wins from Shekhar's father's.

relationship_to_protagonist: His mother, the heiress whose money bought the marriage that displaced Shanti.
relationship_to_romance: No direct part, though her marriage is the transaction the whole film proceeds from.
character_gist: The wealthy heiress Raj Kumar Gupta married in 1953, daughter of Seth Dindayal, who made his son-in-law an equal partner in the business.

relationship_to_protagonist: The principal female part opposite Kapoor's Anand, on a double credit. The article has no plot section, so the relation is undocumented.
relationship_to_romance: Not documented. Romance presence is left blank for the film and no Romances row was created.
character_gist: A double credit as Leela and Julie, matched by Vidya Sinha's Meena and Martha, suggesting a scheme of paired identities the article does not explain.

character_gist: One of two kind-hearted men known to the police for helping capture criminals, searching for the father he has never found, in love with Ruby's friend Neelam, and confronted with the discovery that the killer Kalicharan is his own father.

relationship_to_protagonist: The woman Heeralal meets and loves, and who is united with him at the end.
relationship_to_romance: The pairing recorded in the Romances sheet, and subordinate to the film's crime plot.
character_gist: The woman Heeralal falls in love with, whose friend Neelam takes up with Pannalal, giving the film its two symmetrical couples.

relationship_to_protagonist: No romantic connection to Heeralal; she is Ruby's friend and Pannalal's match.
relationship_to_romance: The parallel romance, resolved with the other at the close.
character_gist: Ruby's friend, who falls in love with Pannalal and is united with him in the ending that pairs off both couples.

relationship_to_protagonist: The killer of his parents, whom he has been hunting without knowing his identity, and who is his partner's father.
relationship_to_romance: No direct part in it.
character_gist: A renowned criminal who sets out to punish the two men for interfering in his business, is driven into flight by the police, and is revealed to be both the murderer of Heeralal's parents and the father Pannalal has been looking for.

relationship_to_protagonist: The commissioner who values the pair's help against criminals and undertakes to protect them from Kalicharan.
relationship_to_romance: No part in it.
character_gist: The police commissioner pleased with the two men's record of helping capture criminals, who sets out to protect them from Kalicharan and Panther, credited with Kamini Kaushal as his wife.

relationship_to_protagonist: Kalicharan's associate in the campaign against the two men.
relationship_to_romance: No part in it.
character_gist: Kalicharan's friend and associate, named with him as the threat the police commissioner sets out to shield the pair from.

relationship_to_protagonist: Wife of the commissioner who protects them, in the household on the law's side of the film.
relationship_to_romance: No part in it.
character_gist: Credited as Mrs. Premlal, wife of the police commissioner who takes the two men under his protection.

relationship_to_protagonist: The landlord's enforcer sent to kill him, who turns out to be his younger brother, is reformed by him, and then betrays him for a bribe and beats him.
relationship_to_romance: Outside Gautam's romance; his own admirer is Gulabo.
character_gist: Rajasahab's trusted henchman, twice sent to kill the new inspector and twice failing, revealed as Gautam's brother born after their father's murder, reformed by him, and turned again by Bagga's bribe into dacoity and the delivery of his brother to the Rajasahab.

relationship_to_protagonist: The village woman whose respect for him becomes love, and the person to whom he finally reveals his identity.
relationship_to_romance: The pairing recorded in the Romances sheet as friendship to love, and secondary to the film's business of oppression and brotherhood.
character_gist: A village belle who develops first respect and then love for the honest inspector on punishment posting, returned in time, and the one he tells the truth to when he comes back to find the village burning.

relationship_to_protagonist: His own mother, from whom he was separated as a child and whose motherly love he wins back before either of them knows the relation.
relationship_to_romance: No part in it; the recognition plot is the film's real centre.
character_gist: Govinda's mother, saved by Gautam during the second attempt on his life, who gives him a mother's affection before he discovers she is his own mother, separated from him when Rajasahab killed their father and she was carrying Govinda.

relationship_to_protagonist: The landlord who killed his father, drove out his predecessors, and orders his death twice.
relationship_to_romance: The external threat over the whole village, and so over the courtship.
character_gist: A Rajasahab whose hold on the villagers is total and who killed Gautam's father for rebelling against his oppression, and who sets his enforcer on the inspector who begins to break that hold.

relationship_to_protagonist: The Rajasahab's younger brother, who destroys Gautam's reputation in his absence by claiming he took a bribe.
relationship_to_romance: No direct part in it.
character_gist: Rajasahab's younger brother, who sows discord in the village while Gautam is away receiving a government award, claiming the inspector took two lakh rupees as a bribe, and buys Govinda with the same currency.

relationship_to_protagonist: No attachment to Gautam; she is the second village woman, paired with his brother.
relationship_to_romance: The film's parallel romance, set beside Gautam and Sandhya.
character_gist: A village belle who admires Govinda, the counterpart on the henchman's side to Sandhya on the inspector's.

relationship_to_protagonist: No part in the plot; billed as a special appearance.
relationship_to_romance: No part in it.
character_gist: A dancer in a special appearance, credited as such in a film otherwise about feudal oppression in a village.

relationship_to_protagonist: The Anglo-Indian girl he seizes from Lala Ramjimal's house and then wants to marry, in the film Kapoor produced himself.
relationship_to_romance: The pairing recorded in the Romances sheet as forbidden love, and forbidden by history: her mother makes the marriage contingent on a British defeat.
character_gist: The daughter of an English priest and a half-Nawabi mother, who escapes the massacre at the church, takes refuge with a Hindu family, is carried off with her mother and grandmother to a Pathan household, and becomes the object of a chieftain's obsession.

relationship_to_protagonist: His wife, watching him install an Englishwoman in their house and fall in love with her.
relationship_to_romance: The pairing recorded in the Romances sheet as a marriage under strain, and the cost of the other one.
character_gist: Javed Khan's wife, who becomes bitterly jealous when her husband brings Ruth Labadoor and her family into their home and turns his attention on the girl.

relationship_to_protagonist: Ruth's mother, and the only person who successfully blocks him: she ties her daughter's hand to the defeat of the British. Kapoor's own wife, in the film he produced.
relationship_to_romance: The obstacle, and a shrewd one: the condition she sets makes the marriage impossible without making refusal look like disloyalty.
character_gist: A widow of English marriage and Rampur Nawabi descent who escapes the church massacre with her daughter and mother, takes refuge with Lala Ramjimal, and extracts from Javed the promise that he may have Ruth only if the British are defeated.

relationship_to_protagonist: His younger brother-in-law, politically awake where Javed is merely reckless, and angry at the Englishwomen in the house until Pathan custom overrides him.
relationship_to_romance: Opposes it from within the household, on the grounds Javed himself ignores.
character_gist: Javed's brother-in-law, an active plotter against the British Empire, who is angered by the presence of the English guests and gives way to the Pathan obligation of sanctuary even to the uninvited.

relationship_to_protagonist: The man whose house Javed barges into to take the women away, and whose silent love for Miriam Javed overrides by force.
relationship_to_romance: The quiet rival, and the film's other divided loyalty.
character_gist: A wealthy Hindu who shelters the three fugitive women, torn between loyalty to India and his privileged position under the British, and silently in love with Miriam, who seems silently to return it.

relationship_to_protagonist: Ruth's grandmother, a Muslim of the Rampur Nawabi family, whose presence complicates every claim made about the household's loyalties.
relationship_to_romance: Part of the family Javed must negotiate with.
character_gist: A Muslim woman of the royal Nawabi family of Rampur who married an Englishman, escaping the massacre with her daughter and granddaughter; played by the Urdu writer Ismat Chughtai.

relationship_to_protagonist: Ruth's father, killed in the church before Javed's part in the story begins.
relationship_to_romance: His death is the condition of the whole encounter.
character_gist: The English priest, Ruth's father, among the British administrators massacred by freedom fighters during Sunday worship.

relationship_to_protagonist: Outside the story, framing it.
relationship_to_romance: No part in it.
character_gist: The film's narrator, setting the story of a Pathan chieftain and an English girl against the Indian Rebellion of 1857.

relationship_to_protagonist: His younger brother, kept in a wealth he believes is real, and left to nurse the crippled man whose whole account of himself then collapses; played by Kapoor's nephew.
relationship_to_romance: Holds the film's romance. Kapoor's own character has none, which is why romance presence is recorded as None.
character_gist: A student at a prestigious college who believes his brother is a prosperous businessman, falls in love with a rich widower's only daughter, undertakes the care of his brother after the lorry accident, and is told by the police that the man was a circus trapeze artiste and a murder suspect.

relationship_to_protagonist: His brother's match, whose marriage he negotiates with her father; no romantic connection to Kapoor's own character.
relationship_to_romance: The film's only romance, and it belongs to the brother.
character_gist: The only daughter of the wealthy widower Gulabchand, in love with Vishal, whose marriage is settled between her father and Karan shortly before her father is killed.

relationship_to_protagonist: The man he settles his brother's marriage with, and whose murder he is then suspected of.
relationship_to_romance: Sanctions the romance and is killed immediately afterwards.
character_gist: A wealthy widower who meets Karan and finalises his daughter's marriage to Vishal, and is killed soon after, a crime of which Karan becomes a suspect.

relationship_to_protagonist: The officer who dismantles Kapoor's character's whole account of himself, telling Vishal what his brother actually is.
relationship_to_romance: Indirect: the revelation lands on the household the marriage was arranged into.
character_gist: The police inspector who informs Vishal that Karan was never a businessman but a trapeze artiste with Amar Circus, and a suspect in a daring robbery and Gulabchand's murder.

relationship_to_protagonist: Belongs to the criminal side of the life Kapoor's character has concealed; the article's synopsis does not detail it.
relationship_to_romance: No part in it.
character_gist: Credited as Rawat, among the antagonists of a plot whose robbery and murder the article's summary raises without resolving.

relationship_to_protagonist: No part in the plot.
relationship_to_romance: No part in it.
character_gist: Credited as a bar dancer, one of the last of the standing cabaret credits Helen held through two decades.

relationship_to_protagonist: His twin, stolen at birth and sold to a bootlegger, who confronts him as a petty criminal, becomes his closest friend, and takes over the investigation when Kishan is blinded.
relationship_to_romance: Outside Kishan's attachments; the article's summary describes neither brother's romance.
character_gist: The twin stolen by Jaggi and sold to the bootlegger Pascal, who raises and educates him into a petty criminal and alcoholic, who clashes with the policeman Kishan, befriends him, is hired by their own unknown father to kill him, warns him instead, and hunts the culprit after Kishan loses his sight.

relationship_to_protagonist: His mother, who raised him alone with great difficulty after one twin was stolen and her husband abandoned her.
relationship_to_romance: No documented part in it.
character_gist: The mother of the twins, who loses one of them to Jaggi's theft and then her husband to abandonment, brings Kishan up with difficulty, and has given up hope of finding the other son.

relationship_to_protagonist: His father, who abandoned the family, does not know his wife and sons are alive, and hires one son to murder the other.
relationship_to_romance: No documented part in it.
character_gist: The twins' father, a criminal whose rivalry with Jaggi cost him one son, who abandoned his wife and, years later and without revealing his identity, hires Amit to kill Kishan at a Navratri dance.

relationship_to_protagonist: The rival gangster who stole and sold his twin, and so the author of the separation the film exists to undo.
relationship_to_romance: No documented part in it.

relationship_to_protagonist: The bootlegger who bought and raised his brother, and so the reason the twins meet as policeman and criminal.
relationship_to_romance: No documented part in it.
character_gist: The bootlegger to whom Jaggi sells the stolen twin, and who exploits and educates the boy into a petty criminal and an alcoholic.

character_gist: Credited as Basanti, third-billed. The article's synopsis covers the twins, their parents and the gangsters, and does not describe her part.
