relationship_to_protagonist: The estate's factory manager, in love with the twin Prem did not court, and one of the three parties investigating separately once Rekha is presumed dead.
relationship_to_romance: A rival interest in the family rather than in Prem's fiancee, and a suspect in the attempt on her.
character_gist: Son of the chief estate manager and the factory's manager, in love with Rashmi against her sister's wishes, and among those searching for the killer after Rekha's supposed death.

relationship_to_protagonist: The chief estate manager who runs the property Prem marries into, and Kishore's father.
relationship_to_romance: Part of the household whose interests the sudden engagement disturbs.
character_gist: The chief estate manager who helps Rekha run the family business after her father's murder, and father of the factory manager in love with her sister.

relationship_to_protagonist: Shelters the woman he is thought to have killed, and so holds the secret the film's second half turns on.
relationship_to_romance: The refuge from it: Rekha comes to her rather than to her fiance.
character_gist: Rekha's friend, whose house the surviving twin reaches after being pushed into the lake, and with whom she plans the investigation into her own death.

relationship_to_protagonist: The twins' father, murdered before Prem appears, whose killing is the crime the film eventually returns to.
relationship_to_romance: No part in it; his death is what leaves the estate and the marriage in play.
character_gist: A Rai Bahadur killed in cold blood in a remote village, survived by twin daughters who inherit the estate and the business.

relationship_to_protagonist: Rekha's police friend, whose arrival at the engagement is the moment Prem is suspiciously found missing.
relationship_to_romance: The first thing that casts doubt on the fiance.
character_gist: Rekha's inspector friend, whose appearance at the engagement to wish the couple well coincides with Prem's unexplained absence.

relationship_to_protagonist: His father, credited with Urmila Bhatt as his mother, the one family the film gives Kapoor's character.
relationship_to_romance: The household on the suitor's side of a marriage the estate regards as beneath it.
character_gist: Credited as Prem's father, with Urmila Bhatt as Prem's mother, in a plot where the suitor's own background is the open question.

relationship_to_protagonist: His sworn enemy among burglars, sent on the same abduction and into the same school under a matching false name; the two end by joining forces.
relationship_to_romance: Holds the parallel romance with the principal's daughter while Kapoor's takes the dance teacher.
character_gist: A petty burglar and sworn rival, sent by his own boss to abduct a rich man's son, who enters the school as the P.E. instructor Ram, grows fond of the boy, abandons the plan, and helps rescue him.

relationship_to_protagonist: The school's dance teacher, who falls in love with the music master he is pretending to be and then talks the criminal out of him.
relationship_to_romance: The pairing recorded in the Romances sheet, and subordinate to the caper: the love is what reforms him rather than what the film is about.
character_gist: The school's dance teacher, unaware of the new music master's background, who falls in love with him and on learning the truth changes him for good by it.

relationship_to_protagonist: No romantic connection to Kapoor's Sunil; she is the principal's daughter and the other burglar's attachment.
relationship_to_romance: The mirror romance, which reforms Vijay as Shalu reforms Sunil.
character_gist: The principal's daughter, who falls in love with the new P.E. instructor without knowing his motive, and helps turn him from the abduction.

relationship_to_protagonist: His own boss, who loses faith in him and carries out the abduction himself, turning employer into enemy.
relationship_to_romance: No part in it.
character_gist: The boss who sends Sunil to abduct Seth Mathur's son, gives up on him when he stalls, kidnaps the boy himself, and is arrested when the two rivals combine against him.

relationship_to_protagonist: His mother, the one domestic tie the film gives him against the criminal life.
relationship_to_romance: No documented part in it.
character_gist: Credited as Sarojini, Sunil's mother, in a film that otherwise keeps both burglars inside their disguises.

relationship_to_protagonist: The principal who appoints him music teacher on a false identity, and Anju's father.
relationship_to_romance: Governs the school where both courtships are conducted.
character_gist: The school principal who hires the two impostors as music and physical-education teachers, and father of Anju.

relationship_to_protagonist: The wealthy father of the boy he is sent to abduct, and so the object of the whole scheme.
relationship_to_romance: No part in it.
character_gist: The rich man whose son Bittoo the two burglars are commissioned to abduct for ransom.

relationship_to_protagonist: One of three childhood friends, a tycoon, cordial to Vijay's family, who becomes his rival over Rekha and over his own father's crimes, and finally dies shielding him.
relationship_to_romance: The competing claim, pressed through his father's marriage proposal, and withdrawn in the end.
character_gist: A tycoon and one of three inseparable friends, son of the criminal Mohanlal Saxena, who loves Rekha, secures her through his father's proposal, misreads Vijay's motives into open rivalry, recognises what his father is, and dies protecting Vijay in penance.

relationship_to_protagonist: The woman all three friends love and who returns Vijay's feeling, then accepts the tycoon out of gratitude when his father clears her own father.
relationship_to_romance: The pairing recorded in the Romances sheet as a triangle, and decided by obligation rather than preference.
character_gist: The woman loved by three childhood friends, who reciprocates Vijay, and accepts Jeet's proposal in gratitude after Jeet's father withdraws the charge against her own father Dinanath.

relationship_to_protagonist: The third of the friends, a policeman, who ends by pursuing the hitman that has framed Vijay for murder.
relationship_to_romance: One of the three suitors, and the one who withdraws without contest.
character_gist: A police officer, the third of the three childhood friends who all love Rekha, and the one who hunts the henchman when Vijay is framed for a woman's murder.

relationship_to_protagonist: Jeet's father, and the man whose crimes set the two friends against each other; he also kills Vijay's brother.
relationship_to_romance: Buys Rekha's consent for his son by clearing her father, making the marriage a transaction.
character_gist: A notorious criminal behind a respectable front, who has his partner killed by a hitman, lets Rekha's father take the blame and then clears him to secure her for his son, and kills the journalist investigating him in a staged accident.

relationship_to_protagonist: His brother, a journalist, whose murder turns Vijay's suspicion into a campaign.
relationship_to_romance: No part in it.
character_gist: Vijay's brother, a candid journalist, who receives the dying hitman's evidence against Saxena, sets out to expose him, and is killed in an engineered accident.

relationship_to_protagonist: Rekha's father, whose false arraignment and later acquittal are the levers by which she is moved from Vijay to Jeet.
relationship_to_romance: The obligation that decides the triangle.
character_gist: Rekha's father, arraigned for the murder actually committed on Saxena's orders, and acquitted when Saxena surrenders the hitman to buy Rekha's gratitude.

relationship_to_protagonist: Saxena's hitman, who frames him for a woman's murder.
relationship_to_romance: No part in it.
character_gist: Saxena's hired killer, who murders his partner, extorts him, absconds with the evidence, is shot, and whose surviving associate incriminates Vijay for the killing of Mona.

relationship_to_protagonist: The woman for whose murder Vijay is framed.
relationship_to_romance: No part in it.
character_gist: The woman whose killing is laid at Vijay's door by Saxena's men, the charge his policeman friend must then unpick.

relationship_to_protagonist: His brother and partner: the two live together in Bombay and run their confidence tricks as a double act, one posing as the policeman the other is being arrested by.
relationship_to_romance: Outside Ravi's courtship of Pushpa, which the two conduct their swindles around.
character_gist: The younger of two estranged brothers of a DCP, intelligent and idle, who cons hotel managers and debtors with his brother until Shakaal's murder of the eldest turns the pair into avengers.

relationship_to_protagonist: His eldest brother, honest and estranged from the two swindlers, whose death is what gives the film its purpose.
relationship_to_romance: No part in it.
character_gist: An upright deputy commissioner transferred to Bombay with his wife and small daughter, estranged from his two con-artist brothers, whose pursuit of Shakaal costs him his life.

relationship_to_protagonist: The criminal who kills his eldest brother and whom the surviving two set out to destroy.
relationship_to_romance: No part in it.
character_gist: The film's bald, island-dwelling criminal mastermind, who kills DCP Shiv Kumar and becomes the object of the brothers' campaign; the part has outlasted the film as a Hindi-cinema archetype.

relationship_to_protagonist: The young woman he is attracted to at the restaurant, met under the name Pushpa and in the middle of a debt that turns out to be part of a swindle of its own.
relationship_to_romance: The pairing recorded in the Romances sheet, and secondary to the revenge plot.
character_gist: A young woman who presents herself as Pushpa Bhargav, owing thirty thousand rupees and offering her Porsche against the debt, the car proving to be stolen and the brothers arrested for buying it.

relationship_to_protagonist: His eldest brother's wife, and after the murder the widow whose claim on the two younger men is the film's moral centre.
relationship_to_romance: No part in it.
character_gist: DCP Shiv Kumar's wife, mother of their daughter Guddi, widowed by Shakaal and left with the brothers-in-law her husband had disowned.

relationship_to_protagonist: Part of the group assembled against Shakaal rather than a connection of Ravi's own.
relationship_to_romance: Outside Ravi's courtship.
character_gist: Credited as Sunita, among the company the brothers gather for the assault on Shakaal's island.

relationship_to_protagonist: Recruited into the mission against Shakaal, and credited with Padmini Kapila as his wife Roma.
relationship_to_romance: No part in Ravi's.
character_gist: Credited as Rakesh, with a wife of his own in the cast list, one of the confederates the brothers assemble to reach Shakaal.

relationship_to_protagonist: The brothers' standing informer, and the one they turn to when they need to know what is going on.
relationship_to_romance: No part in it.
character_gist: A legless but dignified beggar who serves as the brothers' regular informer on shady characters in the city.

relationship_to_protagonist: No part in the plot; credited for the song 'Yamma Yamma'.
relationship_to_romance: No part in it.
character_gist: Credited for the number 'Yamma Yamma', one of the two song appearances the cast list singles out, with Bindu credited as the Maharani of 'Pyaar Karne Wale'.

relationship_to_protagonist: His first wife, fourteen years insensible in an institution, who recovers and comes home to a household rearranged to hide that he has married her sister.
relationship_to_romance: The pairing recorded in the Romances sheet as a marriage under strain: a wife restored to a marriage that has been quietly replaced.
character_gist: Balraj's first wife and Purnima's elder sister, who fell down the stairs on hearing of her own sister's widowhood, spent fourteen years comatose in a Bombay institution, wakes when struck on the head by an inmate, learns the truth, and then feigns madness to release her family from her.

relationship_to_protagonist: His second wife and his first wife's younger sister, widowed young, who stages her own widowhood again to protect the woman she replaced.
relationship_to_romance: The pairing recorded in the Romances sheet as an established relationship: the settled marriage that the other one's recovery makes untenable.
character_gist: Balraj's second wife, sister of his first, whose own husband died soon after their wedding, who married Balraj when Sharada's recovery seemed impossible, and who dresses again as a widow and clears the house to spare her sister the truth.

relationship_to_protagonist: His elder son, Sharada's child, whose engagement opens the film and whose parentage is the first thing the plot discloses.
relationship_to_romance: Holds the younger romance, whose fiancee becomes the one person to see through Sharada's performance.
character_gist: Balraj and Sharada's son, engaged to the doctor Sarita, and raised by the aunt he takes for his mother.

relationship_to_protagonist: His son's fiancee, and the one member of the household who works out what Sharada is doing.
relationship_to_romance: The younger romance, and the film's moral witness.
character_gist: A young doctor engaged to Sagar, who shelters the younger boy while the deception is maintained, and who realises that Sharada is acting her madness in order to leave the family free, and is sworn to secrecy.

relationship_to_protagonist: Father to both of his wives, and so the one figure connected to every part of the arrangement.
relationship_to_romance: Part of the family that permitted the second marriage.
character_gist: Father of both sisters, credited as such, in a household where one daughter's husband has married the other.

relationship_to_protagonist: The doctor who releases his first wife and warns the household she is coming, without telling her what she is coming home to.
relationship_to_romance: Sets the deception in motion by that omission.
character_gist: The physician at the institution, who tells Sharada she has been comatose fourteen years but not that Balraj has married Purnima, and alerts the family to her return.

relationship_to_protagonist: His younger son by Purnima, sent out of the house to keep the pretence, and the child whose escape destroys it.
relationship_to_romance: The living evidence of the second marriage.
character_gist: Balraj and Purnima's small son, sent to stay with Sarita so that the house can be made to look as it did fourteen years earlier, whose escape from the hostel reveals the truth to Sharada.

relationship_to_protagonist: The film's senior revolutionary, first-billed above Kapoor in a five-star ensemble.
relationship_to_romance: Outside Kapoor's own attachments, which the article does not describe.
character_gist: A loyal servant of the kingdom of Ramgarh who discovers the British smuggling out gold and bringing in ammunition, is framed for his raja's murder, escapes a death sentence and forms the band of revolutionaries that multiplies into the armies of Kranti.

relationship_to_protagonist: The film's other leader, in a picture Manoj Kumar also directed.
relationship_to_romance: Outside Kapoor's.
character_gist: The freedom fighter known as Kranti, one of the men who lead the struggle against British rule between 1825 and 1875, in the film Manoj Kumar wrote the part for and directed.

relationship_to_protagonist: A fellow member of the rebellion alongside Kapoor's Shakti.
relationship_to_romance: Not documented.
character_gist: Credited as Karim Khan, among the leaders of the armed struggle the film assembles across religions.

relationship_to_protagonist: The princess of the film's court, paired in the cast list with Bharat rather than with Kapoor's Shakti, their son being separately credited.
relationship_to_romance: Belongs to the other lead's romance, not Kapoor's.
character_gist: A princess who joins the independence struggle, credited with Kunal Goswami as Bharat and Meenakshi's son.

relationship_to_protagonist: Fifth-billed among the women; the article's plot summary covers only the men and does not place her against Kapoor's Shakti.
relationship_to_romance: Not documented, which is why romance presence is left blank for the film and no Romances row was created.
character_gist: Credited as Sureeli, with Preeti Ganguly as her friend. The article's synopsis describes the independence struggle and none of the film's personal relationships.

relationship_to_protagonist: Not documented; the article's plot does not reach the film's younger characters.
relationship_to_romance: Not documented.
character_gist: Credited as Sheetal. The article summarises only the political narrative, leaving the ensemble's personal connections unrecorded.

relationship_to_protagonist: One of the Indian collaborators the rebellion is directed against as much as the British.
relationship_to_romance: No part in it.
character_gist: Credited as Shambhu Singh, among the Indian allies of the British in a film whose villainy is divided between the colonial power and its local partners.

relationship_to_protagonist: Not documented; the article's synopsis does not cover the families of the revolutionaries.
relationship_to_romance: No part in it.
character_gist: Credited as Radha, in the maternal register Nirupa Roy occupied through the period.

relationship_to_protagonist: The raja whose murder begins the story and whose conditional grant of the port to the British is the film's original error.
relationship_to_romance: No part in it.
character_gist: The raja of Ramgarh, who permits the British to use the port for trade on conditions they break, and is found stabbed to death when Sanga comes to report it.

relationship_to_protagonist: The title character on a triple credit, opposite whom Kapoor plays a CBI officer. The article has no plot section, so the relation is undocumented.
relationship_to_romance: Not documented.
character_gist: A triple credit as Vikramjeet Singh, the Krodhi of the title, and Acharya Shraddhanand. With no synopsis in the article the scheme of the three identities is unrecorded.

relationship_to_protagonist: Paired with Kapoor's Kumar Sahni and sharing his surname, with A. K. Hangal and Sulochana Latkar credited as Mr. and Mrs. Sahni; the article has no plot to confirm the arrangement.
relationship_to_romance: The pairing recorded in the Romances sheet, and subordinate to the film's other business, which the article does not describe.
character_gist: Credited as Neera Sahni, the surname shared with Kapoor's CBI officer and with the couple credited as Mr. and Mrs. Sahni, indicating a household the article never sets out.

relationship_to_protagonist: Not documented. The credit doubles the Acharya title that Dharmendra's third identity also carries.
relationship_to_romance: Not documented.
character_gist: Credited as Acharya, a title the film also gives to one of Dharmendra's three identities; the article carries no plot to explain the duplication.

relationship_to_protagonist: Not documented; his second credit is a South Indian Vikramjeet Singh, doubling the name of the title character.
relationship_to_romance: Not documented.
character_gist: Credited as Jagira, and as 'South India's Vikramjeet Singh', a doubling of the protagonist's own name that the article does not explain.

relationship_to_protagonist: Not documented, though Vimi is separately credited as Madhavan's mistress.
relationship_to_romance: Not documented.
character_gist: Credited as Madhavan, with Vimi as his mistress. The article has no plot section.

relationship_to_protagonist: Not documented; billed as a special appearance.
relationship_to_romance: Not documented.
character_gist: Credited as Phoolmati in a special appearance, one of two guest parts by leading actresses in a very large cast.

relationship_to_protagonist: Not documented; billed as a guest appearance, with C. S. Dubey credited as her uncle.
relationship_to_romance: Not documented.
character_gist: Credited as Aarti in a guest appearance, with an uncle of her own in the cast list and no plot in the article to place either.

relationship_to_protagonist: Credited with the surname of Kapoor's character, and with Sulochana Latkar as Mrs. Sahni, so presumably his parents; the article does not confirm it.
relationship_to_romance: Not documented.
character_gist: Credited as Mr. Sahni, with Sulochana Latkar as Mrs. Sahni, the family the surname attaches to Kapoor's CBI officer and to Zeenat Aman's Neera.

relationship_to_protagonist: A double credit matching Kapoor's own pairing of a commoner and a prince, which implies a symmetrical impersonation plot the article never describes.
relationship_to_romance: Not documented. Romance presence is left blank for the film and no Romances row was created.
character_gist: A double credit as Geeta Singh and Princess Shabnam, opposite Kapoor's Kishan and Prince Daulat Singh. The article carries a cast list and no plot.

relationship_to_protagonist: First-billed, and by the credit the authority over a prison the plot evidently passes through.
relationship_to_romance: Not documented.
character_gist: Credited as the jailor and billed ahead of Kapoor. With no synopsis the article leaves the part's function unrecorded.

relationship_to_protagonist: Not documented; Bindu is separately credited as his assistant.
relationship_to_romance: Not documented.
character_gist: Credited as Jaikishan, also styled J.K., with Bindu as his assistant, in a film whose article gives no plot.

relationship_to_protagonist: Not documented.
relationship_to_romance: Not documented.
character_gist: Credited as Shera. The article has no plot section and the function is taken from the actor's standing casting.

relationship_to_protagonist: Not documented; the Singh surname is shared with Kapoor's princely identity.
relationship_to_romance: Not documented.
character_gist: Credited as Chandan Singh, sharing a surname with Kapoor's Prince Daulat Singh in a film the article does not summarise.

relationship_to_protagonist: Not documented.
relationship_to_romance: Not documented.
character_gist: Credited as Abba, in the comic register, in a caper whose plot the article does not record.

relationship_to_protagonist: Not documented beyond her attachment to the antagonist.
relationship_to_romance: Not documented.
character_gist: Credited as the assistant to Ajit's Jaikishan, on the antagonist's side of a plot the article leaves undescribed.

relationship_to_protagonist: The Draupadi of the transposition, married into the family Kapoor's Karan serves against; the two are on opposite sides of the feud.
relationship_to_romance: Romance presence is recorded as Minor for the film and no pairing row was created: the Karna figure's isolation is the point, and Supriya belongs to the brothers.
character_gist: The Draupadi of Benegal's modern transposition, wife within the Puranchand family of industrialists, in a business feud that reproduces the Mahabharata's war between cousins.

relationship_to_protagonist: The Duryodhana figure, the cousin whose side Karan takes and whose patronage defines him.
relationship_to_romance: No part in it.
character_gist: Khubchand's elder son and the Duryodhana of the transposition, whose men accidentally kill his cousin's young son and whose faction Karan serves.

relationship_to_protagonist: The Arjuna figure, and the man who murders Kapoor's Karan in revenge for the death of his brother's child.
relationship_to_romance: No part in it.
character_gist: The Arjuna of the transposition, one of Puranchand's three sons, who murders Karan in reprisal for the killing of Balraj's young son.

relationship_to_protagonist: The lifelong bachelor who brought Karan up as an orphan, and the one figure trying to hold both families together.
relationship_to_romance: No part in it.
character_gist: The Bhishma of the transposition, a lifelong bachelor who raised his late brother's sons and the orphan Karan, gave the family business its foundation, and fails to mediate the feud that destroys both houses.

relationship_to_protagonist: The Krishna figure, moving between the two houses as the feud runs its course.
relationship_to_romance: No part in it.
character_gist: The Krishna of the transposition, the figure whose interventions shape a commercial war between two branches of one industrial family.

relationship_to_protagonist: The Yudhishthira figure, eldest of the three brothers on the side opposing Karan's patrons.
relationship_to_romance: No part in it.
character_gist: The Yudhishthira of the transposition, eldest of Puranchand's sons, in the family whose rivalry with their cousins brings both houses down.

relationship_to_protagonist: The Bhima figure, whose young son's death triggers the reprisal that kills Karan.
relationship_to_romance: No part in it.
character_gist: The Bhima of the transposition, credited with Reema Lagoo as his wife, whose small son is accidentally killed by Dhanraj's men.

relationship_to_protagonist: The Kunti figure, and so in the source the mother of the man Karan is; the skeletons the film brings out of the family cupboard turn on such facts.
relationship_to_romance: No part in it.
character_gist: The Kunti of the transposition, in a film whose disclosures from within the family add to the hatred between the two houses.

relationship_to_protagonist: One of the few characters without a named epic counterpart in the cast list, working inside the industrial world the feud is fought in.
relationship_to_romance: No part in it.
character_gist: Credited as Bhavani Pandey, and among the few parts the cast list does not pair with a Mahabharata name.

relationship_to_protagonist: His younger brother, who marries his pregnant fiancee after his death to shield her, and then spends the film in love with someone else.
relationship_to_romance: Inherits Kapoor's relationship and cannot sustain it; the whole film is the cost of that substitution.
character_gist: A Delhi playwright, orphaned young and close to his older brother, who gives up Chandni to marry the pregnant Shobha after Shekhar's death, settles into a passionless marriage after her miscarriage, and resumes the affair with Chandni years later.

relationship_to_protagonist: His fiancee, carrying his child when he is killed in the 1971 war, and afterwards married to his brother out of obligation.
relationship_to_romance: The pairing recorded in the Romances sheet as tragic lovers, cut off by his death and then displaced into a second marriage she did not choose.
character_gist: Shekhar's fiancee, revealed to be pregnant after his death in the Indo-Pakistani war, married to his brother to spare her the stigma, who loses the child in a car accident and comes genuinely to love the husband she was given.

relationship_to_protagonist: No connection to Kapoor's Shekhar, who dies before the two are introduced; her existence is what his death costs his brother.
relationship_to_romance: The romance displaced by Shekhar's death and resumed as an affair years afterwards.
character_gist: The woman Amit loves and hopes to marry, ended by letter when he marries his brother's fiancee, later married to Dr. Anand, and drawn back into an affair with Amit.

relationship_to_protagonist: No connection to Kapoor's character; he belongs to the second generation of the story.
relationship_to_romance: The husband whose marriage the resumed affair betrays, and the doctor who treated Shobha's miscarriage.
character_gist: The doctor who treats Shobha after the accident and is revealed to have married Chandni, befriended by Amit as a route back to his wife.

relationship_to_protagonist: No connection to Shekhar; billed as a guest appearance.
relationship_to_romance: Threatens to expose the affair, being both the investigating officer and Shobha's protective cousin.
character_gist: Shobha's cousin and the policeman investigating the accident Amit and Chandni cause, protective of her and intending to expose the affair. A guest appearance.

relationship_to_protagonist: Mother of his fiancee, and part of the social pressure that makes the substitute marriage necessary.
relationship_to_romance: The social claim that the unwed pregnancy would have fallen on.
character_gist: Credited as Shobha's mother, on the family side of the scandal Amit's marriage is designed to prevent.

relationship_to_protagonist: His wife, married with a concealed past, and blackmailed over it through most of the marriage before telling him herself.
relationship_to_romance: The pairing recorded in the Romances sheet as a marriage under strain, with the strain wholly imported from before it.
character_gist: A hostel resident who falls in love with Raman, becomes pregnant, attempts suicide, is talked out of it by her roommate, marries the industrialist Kumar, is blackmailed by her friend's husband over photographs, and finally tells her husband everything.

relationship_to_protagonist: The blackmailer of his wife, and the husband of her closest friend, which is what makes the extortion possible.
relationship_to_romance: The external pressure on the marriage, and the film's own moral problem, since he ends by feeling guilt rather than being punished.
character_gist: A struggling photographer who marries Kalpana's roommate Revati and then blackmails Kalpana with photographs of her and Raman, and who is left feeling guilty for it once the truth comes out.

relationship_to_protagonist: The man from his wife's past, whose photographs are the blackmail material, and who later helps her after an accident as a taxi driver.
relationship_to_romance: The prior attachment, and by the end a reduced figure rather than a threat.
character_gist: The man Kalpana loved and was made pregnant by, son of Seth Kalidas, and years later a taxi driver who helps her when she is injured in an accident.

relationship_to_protagonist: His wife's closest friend, who saved her life, and who is married to the man blackmailing her.
relationship_to_romance: The bond that both rescues the marriage and exposes it to attack.
character_gist: Kalpana's hostel roommate, also called Meera Bai, who pulls her out of her despair after the failed suicide attempt and then marries the photographer Shivnath.

relationship_to_protagonist: His father-in-law.
relationship_to_romance: The family behind the marriage.
character_gist: Credited as Amarnath, Kalpana's father, in a film whose crisis is a secret carried into her marriage.

relationship_to_protagonist: His son with Kalpana, credited as such.
relationship_to_romance: The issue of the marriage the blackmail threatens.
character_gist: Credited as Kumar and Kalpana's son, the child of the marriage rather than of the relationship the blackmail concerns.

relationship_to_protagonist: His son, and the film's actual centre: a boy caught between his parents' failing marriage who leaves to become a fighter pilot. Played by Kapoor's own son, in a film Kapoor produced.
relationship_to_romance: Stands outside his parents' marriage and holds the film's own romance, with Anna.
character_gist: A confused teenager caught between a Punjabi father and a Maharashtrian mother whose marriage is failing, who joins the Indian Air Force, learns to fly the MiG-21, courts his instructor's daughter, and comes into his own as a pilot in the 1971 war.

relationship_to_protagonist: His wife, in a marriage whose difficulty is the film's domestic subject and whose differences are drawn along region and religion.
relationship_to_romance: The pairing recorded in the Romances sheet as a marriage under strain, secondary to the son's coming of age.
character_gist: Angad's Maharashtrian Hindu mother, whose marital difficulties with her clean-shaven Sikh husband are the situation their son is trying to find his way out of.

relationship_to_protagonist: No connection to Kapoor's Nihal; she belongs to his son's story.
relationship_to_romance: The film's younger romance, and the one that helps Angad overcome his fear of flying.
character_gist: The daughter of Angad's Malayali Syrian Christian flying instructor, attracted to him and instrumental in his overcoming his fears and realising his potential as a fighter pilot.

relationship_to_protagonist: No dealings with Nihal; he is the authority over the son's new life and the father of the girl.
relationship_to_romance: Governs the younger romance from the woman's side.
character_gist: The chief flying instructor, a Malayali Syrian Christian, who trains Angad and whose daughter he courts.

relationship_to_protagonist: A senior presence in the household whose tensions the film sets out.
relationship_to_romance: Part of the family the marriage strains run through.
character_gist: Credited as Angad's grandmother, in the mixed household the film uses to set Punjabi Sikh against Maharashtrian Hindu.

relationship_to_protagonist: Credited in the world around the family rather than the squadron.
relationship_to_romance: No documented part in it.
character_gist: Credited as Arvind, in an ensemble the film draws from across the parallel-cinema company Kapoor was then producing.

relationship_to_protagonist: Part of the Air Force structure the son enters and the father does not belong to.
relationship_to_romance: No part in it.
character_gist: A wing commander in the squadron Angad joins, one of the officers representing the range of religions the film deliberately assembles.

relationship_to_protagonist: His defence counsel, appointed to save him from a murder charge; the two brothers acting opposite each other, with the eldest playing the title role.
relationship_to_romance: Outside the marriage the murder charge threatens.
character_gist: An ordinary advocate engaged by the judge to defend a sculptor accused of murder, who investigates the case himself and establishes that the killing was done by a steward avenging his own fiancee's past.

relationship_to_protagonist: His wife, and the reason he is suspected: the dead man had been lustful towards her.
relationship_to_romance: The pairing recorded in the Romances sheet, and subordinate to the courtroom plot.
character_gist: The sculptor's wife, towards whom the murdered Prem Oberoi had behaved lustfully, which is what supplies her husband with a motive.

relationship_to_protagonist: The man whose murder he is tried for, and whose conduct towards his wife gave him the motive.
relationship_to_romance: The threat to the marriage, and the corpse the trial is about.
character_gist: A man lustful towards the sculptor's wife, murdered by the steward Suresh Talwar on discovering he had previously been involved with Talwar's fiancee.

relationship_to_protagonist: Not connected to him directly; her past is the actual motive for the killing he is charged with.
relationship_to_romance: No part in his marriage.
character_gist: The steward Suresh Talwar's fiancee, previously involved with Prem Oberoi, and murdered in turn for having witnessed Talwar's crime.

relationship_to_protagonist: The judge who appoints his defence counsel, which is the act that saves him.
relationship_to_romance: No part in it.
character_gist: The judge who engages an ordinary advocate as defence lawyer for the accused sculptor, and before whom the acquittal is obtained.

relationship_to_protagonist: The prosecutor pressing the murder charge against him.
relationship_to_romance: No part in it.
character_gist: Credited as the public prosecutor in the trial of the sculptor Shekhar Kumar.

relationship_to_protagonist: Shares his wife's surname, so presumably her father, though the article does not state it.
relationship_to_romance: The family on the wife's side of the marriage.
character_gist: Credited as Captain Chaudhary, sharing the surname of Kalpana Chaudhary; the article's short synopsis does not set out the relation.

relationship_to_protagonist: The bellboy at his hotel, who turns out to be the son of the man who died protecting his father, and who swears to protect him as his father did.
relationship_to_romance: Outside Raja's romance; his own is with Poonam.
character_gist: The son of Bhim Singh and Savitri, raised by his grandfather in the village believing himself unwanted, who comes to the city as a bellboy in the hotel his mother runs, learns she is his mother and not Raja's, and takes up his father's charge of protecting Raja.

relationship_to_protagonist: The dancer he is attracted to, hired to kill him, who cannot do it and marries him instead.
relationship_to_romance: The pairing recorded in the Romances sheet as damaged by mistrust: the attachment is founded on a commission to murder him.
character_gist: A young dancer engaged by Ranjit Singh to kill Raja, who falls in love with him and cannot carry it out, arranges the boat party meant to finish it, and marries him after the plot is foiled.

relationship_to_protagonist: The woman he has always taken for his mother, who is in fact Arjun's, and who gave up her own son to keep her promise to protect him.
relationship_to_romance: No part in it.
character_gist: Bhim Singh's wife, made trustee of the Singh property and guardian of the infant Raja, blamed by everyone for the deaths of her husband and employer, who hands her own son to his grandfather and passes as Raja's mother to keep him safe.

relationship_to_protagonist: No connection to Raja; she belongs to Arjun's side of the film.
relationship_to_romance: The parallel romance, married off with Raja's at the close.
character_gist: The woman Arjun meets and loves in the city, married to him in the double wedding that closes the film.

relationship_to_protagonist: The manager of his own hotel, plotting his death and turning him against the woman who raised him.
relationship_to_romance: Creates it and corrupts it: he is the one who hires Nisha to kill Raja.
character_gist: Girdhar Singh's son and manager of Raja's hotel, who plots to kill him, frames Savitri so that Raja will suspect her, and hires the dancer Nisha as the instrument.

relationship_to_protagonist: His father's step-brother and killer, and the origin of the whole conspiracy against him.
relationship_to_romance: No part in it.
character_gist: Raja Singh's step-brother, who made repeated attempts on his life and finally killed both him and his bodyguard Bhim Singh on the day the trust was settled.

relationship_to_protagonist: His father's manager and bodyguard, who died alongside him; the charge he laid on his wife is what protected Raja's childhood.
relationship_to_romance: No part in it.
character_gist: Manager and personal bodyguard to Seth Raja Singh, who saved him from many attempts on his life and died with him, extracting from his wife the promise to look after the infant heir.

relationship_to_protagonist: His father, killed at the start, whose property and guardianship arrangements the rest of the film is a fight over.
relationship_to_romance: No part in it.
character_gist: Seth Raja Singh, Raja Kumar's father, who appoints Savitri trustee and guardian and is killed the same day by his step-brother.

relationship_to_protagonist: The smuggler whose daughter wants to marry him, and so the film's question in person: the police officer is the test of what the man values.
relationship_to_romance: The obstacle, and the one the film is actually about resolving.
character_gist: The country's most powerful smuggler, fortified by money and influence, who finds his daughter in love with a police officer and his son engaged to a poor girl, and must decide between his children's happiness and his own power.

relationship_to_protagonist: The smuggler's daughter, in love with him and wanting to marry him across the whole of her father's world.
relationship_to_romance: The pairing recorded in the Romances sheet as a couple united against the external world, the world being her family's business.
character_gist: Dhanpat Rai Mehta's daughter, who falls in love with the police officer Ravi Malhotra and wants to marry him, putting her father's power against his children's happiness.

relationship_to_protagonist: His prospective brother-in-law, defying the same father on the same principle from the other direction; played by Kapoor's nephew.
relationship_to_romance: The parallel defiance: he is engaged to a poor girl as his sister is to a policeman.
character_gist: Mehta's son, who has taken a path opposed to his father's and is engaged to the poor Reshmi, doubling the challenge his sister's romance presents.

relationship_to_protagonist: The smuggler's wife, inside the household both children are defying.
relationship_to_romance: Part of the family the marriage would have to be accepted by.
character_gist: Credited as Anju Mehta, wife of the smuggler whose children have both chosen against his world.

relationship_to_protagonist: No direct connection; she is his prospective brother-in-law's fiancee.
relationship_to_romance: The mirror of his own position: poor where he is honest, and equally unacceptable.
character_gist: A pretty but poor young woman engaged to Vikram Mehta, the second match Dhanpat Rai's money and standing object to.

relationship_to_protagonist: His father, and the household on the honest side of the film's opposition.
relationship_to_romance: The family the smuggler's daughter would be marrying into.
character_gist: Credited as Lala Dinanath Malhotra, father of the police officer, on the modest side of a match with the country's most powerful smuggler.

relationship_to_protagonist: The criminal interest against him inside the smuggler's world.
relationship_to_romance: A threat to the couple rather than an objection to them.
character_gist: Credited as Shamsher Singh, among the criminal apparatus surrounding Dhanpat Rai Mehta's operation.

relationship_to_protagonist: His wife, and a judge, which is what makes the disclosure of a seven-year-old son by another woman a matter of standing as well as of marriage.
relationship_to_romance: The pairing recorded in the Romances sheet as a marriage under strain, and the party the blackmail is aimed at.
character_gist: Prem Kapoor's wife, a judge, mother of Sunil and Babli, who must be faced with a child brought home from Bombay and with the affair a blackmailer is threatening to disclose.

relationship_to_protagonist: The woman he was intimate with seven years earlier, dying of cancer, who summons him to hand over the son he did not know he had.
relationship_to_romance: The pairing recorded in the Romances sheet as forbidden love, and by the time the film opens already over.
character_gist: A woman in Bombay who has known Prem for seven years, mother of his son Bittu, diagnosed with cancer and not expected to live, who asks him to take the boy and leaves for treatment in America.

relationship_to_protagonist: The visitor who brings the letter that begins the film, and then the blackmailer who wants a large sum to keep the affair from his wife and children.
relationship_to_romance: The external pressure on both relationships at once.
character_gist: The man who delivers Sneh's letter to Prem's small-town house, and who later demands a huge sum to keep the truth about Sneh and Bittu from Bhavna and the children.

relationship_to_protagonist: The seven-year-old son he did not know existed, and whom he brings into his own household.
relationship_to_romance: The living consequence of the earlier relationship, and the thing the marriage must absorb.
character_gist: Sneh's seven-year-old son by Prem, taken home by his father to be raised alongside the two children of the marriage.

relationship_to_protagonist: His son by Bhavna, one of the children the blackmailer threatens to tell.
relationship_to_romance: Part of the household the disclosure would break.
character_gist: Prem and Bhavna's son, credited with a Babli in the household that the arrival of a half-brother unsettles.

relationship_to_protagonist: A medical presence around Sneh's illness and the arrangements for the child.
relationship_to_romance: Peripheral to both relationships.
character_gist: Credited as Dr. Shobha, in the Bombay part of a story that turns on a terminal diagnosis.

relationship_to_protagonist: A friend in the small-town world the film opens in.
relationship_to_romance: No part in the blackmail plot.
character_gist: Credited as Ratanpal Singh, in the comic register of a domestic drama about a concealed child.

relationship_to_protagonist: The young Englishwoman who leaves her civil-servant husband for the Nawab, in the 1923 half of the film.
relationship_to_romance: The pairing recorded in the Romances sheet as forbidden love, and forbidden by empire: the scandal is racial and political before it is personal.
character_gist: Newly married to an assistant collector in Satipur, bored by the narrow society of the memsahibs, warned by the doctor's wife that all Indian men are potential rapists, increasingly enthralled by India itself, and drawn to the Nawab of Khatm.

relationship_to_protagonist: No scenes with the Nawab, who belongs to the 1923 story; she investigates it from 1982.
relationship_to_romance: The frame that reconstructs it, and the second woman whose Indian involvement rhymes with Olivia's.
character_gist: An Englishwoman who inherits her great-aunt Olivia's letters and diary, interviews the elderly Harry Hamilton-Paul, and travels to India in 1982 to trace what became of her.

relationship_to_protagonist: The husband whose wife the Nawab takes, and a functionary of the administration that suspects the Nawab of protecting bandits.
relationship_to_romance: The marriage the affair breaks, and an attentive one rather than a cruel one.
character_gist: An assistant collector in the colonial administration at Satipur, an attentive husband apparently much in love with his wife, who urges her to spend the hot summer in Simla and is refused.

relationship_to_protagonist: The Nawab's mother, inside the palace the Englishwoman is drawn into; her second film with Kapoor, eighteen years after Shakespeare Wallah.
relationship_to_romance: The family presence against which the affair is conducted.
character_gist: The Nawab's mother, in the household at Khatm whose hospitality and pomp the British guests are received with while their administration is moving against her son.

relationship_to_protagonist: The Englishman resident in the Nawab's circle, and Olivia's close friend; in old age he is the witness the 1982 story begins with.
relationship_to_romance: The connecting figure, at home in both the Nawab's palace and Olivia's confidence.
character_gist: Olivia's close friend during their years in India and a guest in the Nawab's household, interviewed as an old man by Anne at the start of her investigation.

relationship_to_protagonist: The political agent leading the British case against him, on the suspicion that he shelters bandits for a share of the loot.
relationship_to_romance: The political pressure that makes the affair ruinous.
character_gist: The political agent who with Mr. Crawford leads the British community's manoeuvres against the Nawab of Khatm, suspecting him of colluding with the bandits ransacking the region.

relationship_to_protagonist: No scenes with the Nawab, but she supplies the film's plainest statement of the prejudice he is on the wrong side of; Kapoor's own wife, warning the heroine against Indian men in the film where Kapoor plays one.
relationship_to_romance: The voice of the memsahib society that makes the affair unthinkable.
character_gist: The morbid wife of the racist local doctor, who warns Olivia that all Indian men are potential rapists, in the narrow English society that bores her.

relationship_to_protagonist: No connection to the Nawab; he belongs to Anne's 1982 story, where her involvement with him parallels Olivia's.
relationship_to_romance: The modern echo of it, in the film's other era.
character_gist: Anne's landlord in 1982 India, credited with Ratna Pathak as his wife Ritu and Tarla Mehta as his mother; played by the tabla player Zakir Hussain.

relationship_to_protagonist: His wife, who cannot settle in Canada, suspects him of an affair with his secretary, and takes their son back to India, dividing the family for twenty years.
relationship_to_romance: The pairing recorded in the Romances sheet as a marriage under strain: an emigration failure and a suspicion, rather than a villain.
character_gist: A traditional Indian woman married to a Toronto businessman, unable to fit into the Western life, who separates from him on suspecting an affair with his secretary and returns to India with their son, leaving him the daughter.

relationship_to_protagonist: His son, raised in India not knowing him, brought back to Canada on the pretext that his own father is a family friend needing help.
relationship_to_romance: The consequence of the marriage's failure, and the agent of the family's reassembly.
character_gist: Arun and Shobha's son, taken to India as a boy and told twenty years later that the man whose daughter has been kidnapped is an old family friend, who enlists Renu's help, discovers Arun is his father and Pinky his sister, and delivers the ransom.

relationship_to_protagonist: His daughter, raised by him in Canada, whose kidnapping reunites the divided family.
relationship_to_romance: Holds the film's other and stranger romance, with her own kidnapper.
character_gist: Arun's daughter, kept with him in Canada after the separation, kidnapped by a gang whose psychopathic leader becomes obsessed with her, and who comes to love him before he is shot dead saving her.

relationship_to_protagonist: The kidnapper of his daughter, and by the end the man who dies protecting her.
relationship_to_romance: The film's second romance, between captor and captive, which it ends by treating as genuine.
character_gist: The psychopathic killer who leads the gang that kidnaps Pinky, develops an obsession that becomes mutual, kills his own boss rather than let her be murdered, and is shot several times shielding her from gunfire.

relationship_to_protagonist: Attached to his son's search rather than to him.
relationship_to_romance: Outside the marriage and the kidnapping romance alike.
character_gist: The woman Raju enlists to help find the gang that has taken Pinky, and who fights off the henchmen with him at the end.

relationship_to_protagonist: The head of the gang that took his daughter, and the one who orders her killed.
relationship_to_romance: The obstacle to the kidnapper's own romance, and killed by him for it.
character_gist: The head of the kidnapping gang, who decides Pinky must be killed once Tony gets too close to her, and is killed by Tony instead.

relationship_to_protagonist: His wife, and after his death the person left to hold the joint household together against a swindler.
relationship_to_romance: The pairing recorded in the Romances sheet as an established relationship, and ended early by his death.
character_gist: Prem's wife in a joint household of three brothers who call their home a temple of love, widowed when Prem is killed, and left with her brother-in-law to defend the house against Seth Dharampal's designs.

relationship_to_protagonist: His youngest brother, and the one who takes up the defence of the house after he is killed.
relationship_to_romance: Holds one of the film's younger romances, with Sunita.
character_gist: The youngest of the three brothers, in love with Sunita, who with his widowed sister-in-law takes on the moneylender trying to cheat the family out of their home.

relationship_to_protagonist: His other brother in the joint family.
relationship_to_romance: Holds the film's second younger romance, with Sapna.
character_gist: The middle of the three brothers, in love with Sapna, in the joint household the film sets against a scheming creditor.

relationship_to_protagonist: The creditor who moves against the family as soon as he is dead.
relationship_to_romance: The external threat to the household all three romances belong to.
character_gist: A seth who goes all out to cheat the three brothers' family of their home after Prem's death, and whose designs the widow and the youngest brother set out to thwart.

relationship_to_protagonist: His youngest brother's attachment, and the daughter of one of the film's antagonists.
relationship_to_romance: A younger romance complicated by her father's position.
character_gist: Ravi's love interest, daughter of Prem Chopra's Sahu, one of the two younger couples in the household.

relationship_to_protagonist: A friend of the family, credited as such.
relationship_to_romance: No part in it.
character_gist: Credited as Prem's family friend, on the household's side of its fight with the seth.

relationship_to_protagonist: Sunita's father, and part of the interest ranged against the family.
relationship_to_romance: The obstacle to his brother's romance.
character_gist: Credited as Sahu, Sunita's father, on the opposing side of the property conflict his daughter's romance crosses.

relationship_to_protagonist: Kapoor's part is a cameo as a doctor; the article's one-sentence description of the film does not connect them.
relationship_to_romance: Not documented, and romance presence is recorded as None for Kapoor's character.
character_gist: Credited as Kavita, first among the women in a film the article summarises in a single sentence about a widower, a run of luck, and a new bride who resembles his late wife and may not mean him well.

relationship_to_protagonist: Shares the medical profession of Kapoor's Dr. Kailash; with only one sentence of plot in the article the connection is undocumented.
relationship_to_romance: Not documented.
character_gist: Credited as Dr. Kanchan, the second doctor in a cast where Kapoor's cameo is also a physician. The article gives no plot beyond its one-line premise.

relationship_to_protagonist: Not documented; the article's single sentence of plot names no character.
relationship_to_romance: Not documented.
character_gist: Credited as Sanjay, in one of his earliest films. The article carries a one-sentence premise and no further plot.

relationship_to_protagonist: The courtesan Kapoor's Samsthanak pursues and cannot have, in a film Kapoor produced and in which he plays the obstacle rather than the lover.
relationship_to_romance: The film's romance belongs to her and Charudutt; Kapoor's character is the pursuer outside it, which is why romance presence is left blank for him and no pairing row was created.
character_gist: A celebrated courtesan of Ujjain whose chance meeting with a poor Brahmin becomes the film's love story, and who is the object of the king's brother-in-law's unwanted attention.

relationship_to_protagonist: The poor Brahmin who has what Kapoor's Samsthanak wants, which makes him the rival at the film's centre.
relationship_to_romance: The romance itself, opposite Vasantsena.
character_gist: A poor Brahmin of Ujjain whose chance meeting with the courtesan Vasantsena becomes a love affair, set against the pursuit of her by a powerful man.

relationship_to_protagonist: Outside the pursuit, and doubling as the film's narrator.
relationship_to_romance: Frames it: the author of the Kamasutra observing a story of courtesans and lovers.
character_gist: Vatsayana, author of the Kamasutra, who also narrates the film, watching the Ujjain of courtesans, thieves and lovers that the story is set in.

relationship_to_protagonist: No part in Samsthanak's pursuit; she belongs to the Brahmin's household.
relationship_to_romance: The wife the romance is conducted against.
character_gist: Credited as Aditi, in the household of the poor Brahmin whose affair with a courtesan the film follows.

relationship_to_protagonist: Belongs to the courtesan's household rather than to Samsthanak's.
relationship_to_romance: Part of the world the central romance moves through.
character_gist: Credited as Madanika, among the women of the courtesan's establishment in Ujjain.

relationship_to_protagonist: Credited in Samsthanak's orbit, as the instrument of his will.
relationship_to_romance: A threat to the couple on the pursuer's behalf.
character_gist: Credited as Sajjal, attached to the powerful Samsthanak in his pursuit of the courtesan.

relationship_to_protagonist: Outside the pursuit; Kapoor's son again, in a film Kapoor produced, with Kulbhushan Kharbanda credited as Aryak's teacher.
relationship_to_romance: No part in it.
character_gist: Credited as Aryak, with a teacher of his own in the cast list, played by Kapoor's elder son in his father's own production.

relationship_to_protagonist: No documented part in the pursuit; Kapoor's daughter, making this the second of her father's productions she appears in after Junoon.
relationship_to_romance: Part of the courtesan household the romance belongs to.
character_gist: Credited as a courtesan's slave, played by Kapoor's daughter, who had appeared as a child in his production of Junoon five years earlier.

relationship_to_protagonist: The businesswoman who travels to Kashmir to evict him from her land and falls in love with him instead.
relationship_to_romance: The pairing recorded in the Romances sheet as rivals to lovers: the relationship begins as a property dispute between families with a history.
character_gist: A wealthy Delhi businesswoman who goes to Kashmir to take possession of land occupied by Suraj Arora, learns from her nanny that the Aroras raised her before her father grew rich and cut them off, falls in love with him, and finds her friend and employee in love with him too.

relationship_to_protagonist: The other woman in love with him, and her rival's own friend and employee.
relationship_to_romance: The competing claim, and the source of the competitiveness the article says changes everyone's lives.
character_gist: Aarti's friend and employee, who also falls in love with Suraj, creating the complications and competition between the two women that the film turns on.

relationship_to_protagonist: The nanny who tells Aarti that his family raised her, which is what turns the eviction into a reconciliation.
relationship_to_romance: Supplies the history that makes the romance possible.
character_gist: Aarti's nanny, who tells her she was brought up by the Arora family until her father grew wealthy and broke off all relations with them.

relationship_to_protagonist: Aarti's father, who cut off the family that raised his daughter once he became rich.
relationship_to_romance: The original rupture between the two families that the romance repairs.
character_gist: Aarti's father, who became wealthy and severed all relations with the Arora family that had brought his daughter up.

relationship_to_protagonist: Of his own family, the Aroras who raised the woman now come to evict them.
relationship_to_romance: The household on his side of the reconciliation.
character_gist: Credited as Karuna Arora, of the family that raised Aarti before her father's wealth separated them.

relationship_to_protagonist: Comic support in the Kashmir setting where the land dispute becomes a courtship.
relationship_to_romance: No part in the rivalry between the two women.
character_gist: Credited as Badal, in the comic register of a film about a disputed piece of Kashmiri land.

relationship_to_protagonist: A senior figure in the Kashmir community around him.
relationship_to_romance: No documented part in it.
character_gist: Credited as Masterji, in the Kashmiri world Suraj Arora occupies and Aarti arrives into.

relationship_to_protagonist: His wife, widowed in the opening movement and raped by his killer, who then drives the whole of the rest of the film.
relationship_to_romance: The pairing recorded in the Romances sheet as tragic lovers, ended in the first minutes and avenged for the remaining length of the film.
character_gist: The wife of the inspector Balvir kills, brutally raped by him afterwards, who is left with the single purpose of revenge and hires two men to bring Balvir to her alive.

relationship_to_protagonist: The biker-gangster he arrests and who kills him for it, in the sequence that ends Kapoor's part.
relationship_to_romance: Destroys it, and then assaults the widow.
character_gist: A notorious biker-gangster arrested by Inspector Ranjit Singh, who kills him and then rapes his wife, and whom she spends the film having hunted.

relationship_to_protagonist: No scenes with Kapoor's inspector, who is dead before he is hired; he is the instrument of the revenge.
relationship_to_romance: Acts on the widow's behalf.
character_gist: One of the two men Sheela hires to capture Balvir alive and deliver him to her, called Raghu.

relationship_to_protagonist: As with Raghu, engaged after Kapoor's character is killed.
relationship_to_romance: Acts on the widow's behalf.
character_gist: The second of the two men Sheela hires to take Balvir alive, called Ballu, credited with Paintal as his friend Nandu.

relationship_to_protagonist: No documented connection to Kapoor's inspector; she is credited with Om Shivpuri as her father.
relationship_to_romance: Belongs to the younger strand rather than to the marriage the film opens with.
character_gist: Credited as Meena Kapoor, with Om Shivpuri as Mr. Kapoor, in the part of the film that follows the two hired men.

relationship_to_protagonist: No documented connection; credited with Sulochana Latkar as his mother Salma.
relationship_to_romance: Outside it.
character_gist: Credited as Jaanu, with Kaajal Kiran as Banu and Sulochana Latkar as his mother, in the film's younger strand.

relationship_to_protagonist: Paired with Kapoor's CID inspector. The article has no plot section, so the course of the relationship is undocumented.
relationship_to_romance: The pairing recorded in the Romances sheet as manipulated by outsiders; the article supplies no account of it.
character_gist: Credited as Advocate Bhavna Bharadwaj, with Gajanan Jagirdar as her father Brahmprakash, in a cast full of advocates. The article carries a long cast list and no synopsis.

relationship_to_protagonist: Second-billed opposite Kapoor's inspector; the relation is not documented.
relationship_to_romance: Not documented.
character_gist: Credited as Bajrang, also called Babua. The article has no plot section.

relationship_to_protagonist: Shares the surname of Kapoor's Ravi Malhotra, which indicates a family relation the article does not confirm.
relationship_to_romance: Not documented.
character_gist: Credited as Kalpana Malhotra, the surname shared with Kapoor's CID inspector. With no synopsis the article leaves the relation unstated.

relationship_to_protagonist: Not documented; one of several advocates in a cast built around a courtroom.
relationship_to_romance: Not documented.
character_gist: Credited as Advocate Devilal, the performance voiced by Amrish Puri, in one of Madan Puri's last films. The article gives no plot.

relationship_to_protagonist: Not documented.
relationship_to_romance: Not documented.
character_gist: Credited as Dayashankar, called Daddu. The article has no plot section.

relationship_to_protagonist: Father of the advocate paired with Kapoor's character, by the credit.
relationship_to_romance: Not documented.
character_gist: Credited as Brahmprakash Bharadwaj, father of Advocate Bhavna Bharadwaj, in a film the article does not summarise.

relationship_to_protagonist: Not documented.
relationship_to_romance: Not documented.
character_gist: Credited as Akbar Lala, a truck driver. The article carries no plot section.
